case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 166/86, decided on 4 September 1987

clause.text: No person shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was subjected to torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment in violation of Article 11 of the Constitution during his arrest and detention.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed he was repeatedly assaulted and tortured by security personnel during unlawful detention and forced to make a statement under duress.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents denied the allegations of torture and assault, and stated the petitioner was lawfully detained under Emergency Regulations and that no inducement or threats were made to obtain statements.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested on 28.7.86 and detained until 18.9.86.
Petitioner alleged repeated assault and forced statement during detention.
No medical evidence was presented to corroborate claims of torture.
Respondents denied assault and claimed lawful detention under Emergency Regulations.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that to establish a violation of Article 11, credible and corroborated evidence of torture or cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment is required.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since the petitioner's allegations of torture were uncorroborated by medical evidence and denied by respondents, the court found the evidence insufficient to prove a violation of Article 11.
principles_established: Allegations of torture under Article 11 require corroboration, such as medical evidence.
Uncorroborated claims are insufficient to establish violation of Article 11.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner did not establish a violation of Article 11 as the evidence was insufficient.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 11 was central to the petitioner's claim of torture and cruel treatment during detention, but the court found insufficient evidence to uphold this claim.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: Petitioner's complaint of torture was not corroborated by medical evidence and was denied by respondents; court found evidence insufficient to establish violation of Article 11.
